claims.value: other: epithelial-like cell in a single, tightly joined layer
claims.quote: These glial cells appear similar to epithelial cells, making a single layer of cells with little intracellular space and tight connections between adjacent cells.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: These glial cells appear similar to epithelial cells, making a single layer of cells with little intracellular space and tight connections between adjacent cells.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Cilia on the cell's apical surface help move cerebrospinal fluid through the ventricles.
claims.quote: They also have cilia on their apical surface to help move the CSF through the ventricular space.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: At the choroid plexus, ependymal cells contact blood vessels and filter and absorb components of the blood to produce cerebrospinal fluid.
claims.quote: The choroid plexus is a specialized structure in the ventricles where ependymal cells come in contact with blood vessels and filter and absorb components of the blood to produce cerebrospinal fluid.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Because they contact blood vessels and filter blood components to make cerebrospinal fluid, ependymal cells can be counted as part of the blood-brain barrier, or as a place where that barrier breaks down.
claims.quote: ependymal cells come in contact with blood vessels and filter and absorb components of the blood to produce cerebrospinal fluid. Because of this, ependymal cells can be considered a component of the BBB, or a place where the BBB breaks down.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Ependymal cells surround blood capillaries and filter the blood to make cerebrospinal fluid.
claims.quote: Ependymal cells (one of the types of glial cells described in the introduction to the nervous system) surround blood capillaries and filter the blood to make CSF.

source.section: 13.3 Circulation and the Central Nervous System
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Lining the fluid-filled ventricles of the brain and the central canal of the spinal cord, ependymal cells help produce the cerebrospinal fluid that cushions the brain.
claims.quote: Ependymal cells line fluid-filled ventricles of the brain and the central canal of the spinal cord. They are involved in the production of cerebrospinal fluid, which serves as a cushion for the brain

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

tier1.text: A neuroepithelial glial cell, derived from a radial glial cell originating from the neuroectoderm, lines the ventricles of the brain and the central canal of the spinal cord. This cell is characterized by the presence of cilia on its apical surface, which can be motile or non-motile.
tier1.attribution: Definition from the Cell Ontology (CL 2026-06-08), CL:0000065. CC BY 4.0.
